user.title: Climate Circuits
user.description: Decides the house mode and runs heating and cooling circuits. Add a circuit for every pump or mixing valve after setup.

data_description.capabilities: A gas boiler only heats; a reversible heat pump heats and cools.
data_description.mode_entity: Climate (hvac mode), select or sensor (values below), or a switch/binary sensor (on = heating). Optional.
data_description.heat_values: Only for select, input_select and sensor sources.

fallback.name: Fallback when the source is unavailable

data_description.kind: Tank: warm water means heating. Outdoor: cold outside means heating.
data_description.heat_threshold: Tank: heat at or above. Outdoor: heat at or below.
data_description.cool_threshold: Tank: cool at or below. Outdoor: cool at or above.

zone_control.name: Zone thermostats
zone_control.description: On a mode change the thermostats of the other mode are turned off first; the new ones are switched on once all of those report off. A thermostat of the other mode that comes on later is turned off again. Only while Control equipment is on.

hot_water.name: Hot water circulation
hot_water.description: Circulation pump with hysteresis: starts below threshold − delta, stops at the threshold. Leave empty if the house has no circulation.

data_description.circulation_sensor: Temperature at the end of the circulation loop.
data_description.threshold: Can also be changed on the Hot water device.

data_description.info_sensors: Their values appear in the attributes of the mode sensor, e.g. hot water, tank or heat pump supply.

protection.name: Protections
protection.description: Pause between heating and cooling, periodic exercise of idle pumps and valves, and homing the valves at the start. Only while Control equipment is on.

data.mode_pause: Pause when switching between heating and cooling
data.exercise_days: Exercise idle pumps and valves after
data.home_mixers_on_start: Home mixing valves when Home Assistant starts

data_description.mode_pause: Minutes the new mode waits after the other one stopped. Going back to the previous mode needs no pause.
data_description.exercise_days: Days without running; 0 turns exercising off.
data_description.home_mixers_on_start: Close every valve against its end stop about 30 s after Home Assistant starts, as the position may have changed while it was down. Takes one full travel; off keeps the saved position. Not on a reload of the integration.

error.no_capabilities: Select at least one mode the source can do.
error.fallback_sensor_required: The fallback needs a temperature sensor.
error.circulation_needs_sensor_and_pump: Circulation needs both the temperature sensor and the pump.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Climate Circuits is already set up.

user.title: Circuit
user.description: One pump and mixing valve with its zones and weather curves.

data_description.heating_zones: Without thermostats for a mode the circuit runs whenever the house is in that mode.
data_description.humidity_sensors: Used for the dew point while cooling.

data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature the system is designed for, e.g. −15 °C.
data_description.design_supply: Water temperature needed at the design outdoor temperature.
data_description.exponent: Radiators 1.3, floor heating 1.1. Higher bends the curve more.

outputs.name: Outputs
outputs.description: Controlled only while Control equipment is on; otherwise decisions are shown in Activity as a dry run.

data_description.mixer_position: Cover of the old integration; its position is used only as a first guess until the valve is homed.
data_description.pump_delay: Seconds of demand before the pump starts, so the zone valves can open.
data_description.pump_run_on: Seconds the pump keeps running after heating demand ends.
data_description.source: Where the circuit takes its water from. With a single heat source in the house it is used even when none is chosen.

mixer.name: Mixer regulation
mixer.description: How the valve regulates the water temperature after the mixer. The defaults suit most radiator and floor circuits.

data_description.travel: Seconds the actuator needs from fully closed to fully open (on its label).
data_description.hysteresis: The valve stays while the water after the mixer is within ± this of the target.
data_description.settle: Seconds to wait after a valve move before the next one, until the changed water reaches the supply sensor. Longer if the valve swings, shorter if it is slow to reach the target.
data_description.gain: How far the valve moves for each °C the water is off the target. Larger reaches the target faster but may overshoot.
data_description.min_step: A smaller move would not change the water noticeably.
data_description.max_step: Limits a single move far from the target.
data_description.trend_window: Seconds of supply readings the direction of the temperature is taken from. When it is heading for the target, the valve waits.
data_description.source_compensation: When the source temperature changes, move the valve at once so the water after the mixer stays the same, without waiting for the supply sensor.
data_description.min_source_gap: The source must be at least this much warmer than the water after the mixer; with a smaller difference sensor noise would move the valve too much.

error.mixer_needs_both_relays: A mixing valve needs both the open and the close relay.
error.mixer_relays_same: The open and close relay must differ.
error.mixer_needs_supply_sensor: A mixing valve needs the supply temperature sensor.

error.mixer_min_step_above_max: The smallest step is larger than the largest step.

user.title: Heat source
user.description: A buffer tank, boiler or heat pump the circuits take their water from. Its temperature lets the mixing valves react at once when the source warms up or cools down.

data.name: Name
data.temperature_sensor: Temperature of the water it gives

data_description.temperature_sensor: The water that goes to the circuits: for a buffer tank its outlet pipe to the mixers; for a boiler or heat pump its supply.
data_description.setpoint_entity: What the source is set to give, e.g. the heat pump's target for the tank (a climate's target temperature, or a number or sensor). Used to warn when a circuit wants more than the source can give.
